items.basis: BOFiP lists the usual straight-line rates 'admis pour la généralité des professions', given 'à titre purement indicatif': 'B. Matériel et outillage … Matériel 10 à 15; Outillage 10 à 20'. Tax depreciation follows the actual useful life component by component; declining balance (CGI art. 39 A) is allowed for certain new assets with life > 3 years (PwC).
items.scope: industrial plant and machinery ('matériel'), straight-line usual rate range
items.notes: A range, not one rate: 10% = 10-year life, 15% = 6.67 years. PwC FR page gives no rate.

items.basis: DM 31 dicembre 1988 (Min. Finanze), Gruppo VII Industrie manifatturiere metallurgiche e meccaniche, Specie II (fabbriche di macchine industriali …; Specie III–V 'Vedi SPECIE II'): 'Impianti generici … e specifici 10%'; 'Grandi impianti e macchine operatrici automatici 15,5%'; 'Attrezzatura varia e minuta 25%'. Maximum IRES rates; half rate in the first year (PwC).
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, automatic machines in the mechanical-engineering sector (generic/specific plant 10%)
items.notes: Rates differ by sector (Gruppo/Specie); 15.5% is the automatic-machine line, 10% the generic and specific plant line.

items.basis: Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, art. 12.1.a) table: 'Maquinaria — Coeficiente lineal máximo 12% — Periodo de años máximo 18'.
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, machinery (minimum 1/18 = 5.56% a year)
items.notes: Declining balance also allowed except buildings/furniture (PwC).

items.basis: Decreto Regulamentar 25/2009 maximum rates as quoted by PwC: 'Engines and machine tools 12.50'; +25% for two shifts, +50% for three shifts.
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, engines and machine tools
items.notes: Statute named from PwC context (maximum rates); national table not opened.

items.basis: Income Taxes Act 586/1992 Coll. §30: depreciation group 2 'Engines, motor vehicles, machines …' minimum period 5 years (PwC table). 100/5 = 20% average; the statutory straight-line split is 11% in year 1 and 22.25% in years 2–5 (§31, not read on a page).
items.scope: group 2 machines, straight-line over the 5-year minimum period
items.notes: The 11% / 22.25% year split is from the Act as remembered, not from an opened page — verify before using the year profile.

items.basis: Income Tax Act 595/2003 Coll.: depreciation group 2 'Combustion engines, outboard engines, most production line equipment, furniture' — 6 years (PwC table). Derived 100/6 = 16.67% a year.
items.scope: group 2 production-line equipment, straight-line over 6 years
items.notes: Accelerated method allowed for groups 2 and 3.

items.basis: ZDDPO-2 (Corporate Income Tax Act) maximum straight-line rates: category 3 'Equipment, vehicles, and machinery 20' (PwC table).
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, equipment and machinery

items.basis: Law on Corporate Income Tax, Annex 1 depreciation periods: 'Plant and machinery 5' years (PwC). Derived 100/5 = 20%.
items.scope: plant and machinery, straight-line over 5 years
items.notes: Double-declining balance also permitted.

items.basis: Corporate Income Tax Act, art. 55: category II 'Machinery, production facilities, apparatuses' maximum rate 30 (50 for new qualifying assets) — PwC table. Only straight-line for tax.
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, category II machinery
items.notes: 50% for new category II assets meeting conditions.

items.basis: §7 EStG: straight-line over the useful life; no rate is prescribed for machinery (only buildings 2.5% and cars 12.5% are). Declining balance up to 30% a year is allowed for assets acquired after 30 June 2020 (Konjunkturstärkungsgesetz 2020).
items.scope: useful-life straight-line; no statutory machinery rate
items.notes: Not found as a fixed rate: Austria taxes on the asset's useful life. Alternative: 30% declining balance.

items.basis: Administrative rates (PwC): 'Machinery and equipment (depending on the type) 20 or 33'. Straight-line; the rate is otherwise agreed with the tax authority on expected life.
items.notes: 33% for shorter-lived equipment.

items.basis: Wet Vpb 1969 art. 8 / Wet IB 2001 art. 3.30: 'the tax depreciation of other fixed assets (i.e. inventory, equipment) is limited to 20% of the purchase price or production costs per annum' (PwC).
items.scope: maximum annual depreciation of equipment (any sound method, capped at 20% of cost)

items.basis: Inkomstskattelagen ch. 18: machinery follows book depreciation provided net value is not below the 30% declining-balance rule or 'cost less 20% per year (i.e. 20% straight-line depreciation on remaining assets)'; alternative 25% declining balance without book conformity (PwC).
items.scope: straight-line complementary rule for machinery and equipment
items.notes: Main rule is 30% declining balance on the pool; 20% straight-line is the complementary rule.

items.basis: Fiscal Code + Government Decision HG 2139/2004 (Catalogue of fixed assets): 2.1.5.2 'Strunguri … Masini de alezat. Masini de frezat … Masini agregat; linii automate … centre de prelucrare a metalului prin aschiere … masini de turnat' 8–12 years; 2.1.5.1 presses, forging machines, 'Masini … de confectionat autovehicule' 9–15 years. Straight-line over a life chosen in the range = 8.33–12.5% (lathes/machining centres) or 6.67–11.1% (presses).
items.source: https://avocatnet.ro/articles/download/8cd069700830f1798cf59f99d6a913c6 (subgroup 2.1 of the catalogue, reproduced by avocatnet); https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/romania/corporate/deductions
items.kind: statute (government decision, reproduced by a legal portal)
items.scope: metal-cutting machine tools and machining centres, straight-line
items.notes: Read from a legal portal's copy of the catalogue, not Monitorul Oficial. Accelerated: up to 50% in year 1 for machinery (Fiscal Code).

items.basis: CIT Law art. 10a + Pravilnik (2019) on classifying fixed assets: five groups at 2.5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30% straight-line (groups II–V straight-line for assets acquired from 2019).
items.kind: advisory summary (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries) + audit firm guide (RSM Serbia)
items.scope: group rates; group of general machinery not found
items.notes: Not found: which group holds general production machinery (annex not opened). Cars are group III (15%).

items.basis: Tax Procedure Law (VUK) art. 315 + General Communiqué No. 333 useful-life list: section 32 (machines in metal goods and machinery manufacturing) 20 years, 5% — read only in a search summary of a GİB ruling, not on the list.
items.notes: Not confirmed on a page: GİB's list page is a JS app and the reproduced lists did not render. Declining balance at 2× the straight-line rate (max 50%) also allowed (PwC).

items.basis: IRC §168 (MACRS): most manufacturing machinery is 7-year GDS property, recovered by 200% declining balance switching to straight-line; a straight-line election over the recovery period gives 100/7 = 14.29% a year (before the half-year convention). ADS (straight-line over class life, e.g. 12 years for Rev. Proc. 87-56 classes 34.0 / 37.11) is the alternative. 100% bonus depreciation applies to property acquired after 19 Jan 2025 (OBBBA) unless elected out.
items.kind: statute (IRS publication) + advisory summary (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries)
items.notes: Class lives in Pub 946 Table B-2 are an image and were not read: the 7-year GDS / 12-year ADS figures for classes 34.0 and 37.11 are from memory — verify.
items.method: 200% declining balance by default; straight-line by election

items.basis: Income Tax Regulations s.1100(1)(a): Class 43 '30 per cent', Class 53 '50 per cent'; Schedule II Class 53 = manufacturing & processing property 'acquired after 2015 and before 2026', so M&P machinery acquired in 2026 falls to Class 43 (30% declining balance, half-year rule). A 100% first-year CCA applies to M&P equipment acquired after 2024 and available for use before 2030 (PwC).
items.scope: declining balance only (capital cost allowance pools)
items.notes: No straight-line rate exists for machinery in Canada.

items.basis: Ley del ISR art. 35 fr. IV: '8% en la fabricación de vehículos de motor y sus partes; … en la fabricación de productos de metal, de maquinaria y de instrumentos profesionales y científicos'; fr. V 9% for rubber and plastic products; fr. XIV 10% other activities.
items.scope: straight-line, machinery used in motor-vehicle / metal-products manufacturing
items.notes: Text 'Última Reforma DOF 01-04-2024'. Deduction is inflation-indexed (NCPI).

items.basis: RFB rates (IN RFB 1700/2017 Annex III): 'The annual rates provided by the RFB normally allowable are 10% for machinery, equipment, furniture, and installations'; +50% for two shifts, +100% for three shifts (PwC).
items.notes: Instruction number named from memory, not on the page.

items.basis: Ordinance on Useful Lives of Depreciable Assets (MOF Ordinance No. 15 of 1965), Appended Table 2: 'Metal products manufacturing equipment — other equipment 10' years; 'Transport equipment manufacturing equipment 9'; 'Plastic products manufacturing equipment 8'. Straight-line 100/10 = 10% (9 years: table rate 0.112).
items.notes: 200% declining balance also allowed for machinery. The 9-year 0.112 rate is from Appended Table 8 as remembered.

items.basis: Enforcement Rule of the Corporate Tax Act, Annex 6 (standard useful lives by industry): C25 fabricated metal products manufacturing 10 years (elective 8–12) — read in a search summary of a tax-tribunal excerpt; PwC: machinery 'from four years … to 20 years' by industry, ±25% election.
items.notes: Annex 6 not opened. Straight-line or declining balance for machinery.

items.basis: Fixed Assets Useful Life Table (MOF order 台財稅字第10604512060號, 3 Feb 2017), class 3: 31002 metal products manufacturing equipment 'other' 8 years; 31303 motor-vehicle manufacturing equipment 10; 31102 CNC machine tools (machinery manufacturing) 5; 31403 industrial robots 2. Lives are MINIMA (rate = maximum): 100/8 = 12.5%.
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, metal products manufacturing equipment
items.notes: Motor-vehicle manufacturing equipment: 10 years = 10%.

items.basis: Royal Decree No. 145 (Revenue Code s.65 bis): 'Other assets not mentioned above, excluding land and inventory — maximum permitted rate 20' (PwC).
items.scope: maximum rate of cost, machinery (other assets)

items.basis: Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC Appendix I (as translated by JETRO): B-1 machine tools 7–15 years; B-6 metallurgical / metal coating equipment 7–15; B-18 other business machinery 5–12. Straight-line over a life chosen in range: 100/15–100/7 = 6.67–14.29%.
items.notes: JETRO page dated 12 Jun 2020; check Circular 45/2013 is still the governing table in 2026 (PwC: 'Depreciation in excess of the rates specified in the regulations … is not deductible').

items.basis: Income Tax Act 1967 Sch. 3 / Income Tax (Qualifying Plant Annual Allowances) Rules: 'General plant and machinery — Initial allowance 20, Annual allowance 14' (heavy machinery 20/20) — PwC table.
items.scope: annual allowance on cost (plus 20% initial allowance in year 1)
items.notes: Year 1 = 20% IA + 14% AA; cost written off in 6 years.

items.basis: Income Tax Law art. 11 + PMK 72/2023 annex: Group 3 (16 years: 6.25% straight-line / 12.5% declining) covers 'Industri mesin — Mesin yang menghasilkan/memproduksi mesin menengah dan berat (misalnya mesin mobil …)' and chemical/plastics machinery; unlisted non-building assets default to Group 3. Group 2 (8 years, 12.5%) covers light-machine industry.
items.scope: straight-line, heavy/medium machinery manufacturing and unlisted machinery
items.notes: Date is the regulation year (exact date not read).

items.basis: No statutory rate: 'Depreciation is generally computed on a straight-line basis … over the asset's useful life … tax depreciation should conform to book depreciation' (PwC; NIRC s.34(F)).
items.notes: Not found as a fixed rate (none exists).

items.basis: Income Tax Act 1947 s.19A: accelerated allowance on all machinery and equipment 'in equal instalments over three years' (100/3 = 33.33%); s.19 alternative straight-line over the Sixth Schedule working life (PwC).
items.scope: straight-line over 3 years (the election nearly all businesses use)
items.notes: 100% in year 1 for computers, robots and prescribed automation equipment.

items.basis: Indicative rates from tax administrative guidelines (PwC table): 'Production equipment, tools, and construction fittings 10 to 15'. Straight-line or declining balance.
Decree 2008-492: 'Equipment and machinery … maximum depreciation rate of 15%, according to the straight-line method'; ×1.5 for manufacturing equipment used ≥16 h/day, ×2 for 24 h/day (PwC).
items.scope: maximum straight-line rate, equipment and machinery

items.basis: Income Tax Law 91/2005 art. 25: 'All others assets are depreciated at a rate of 25% … on a declining-balance method'; optional 30% accelerated first-year allowance on industrial machines (PwC).
items.notes: No straight-line rate for machinery.

items.basis: Income Tax Act s.12C: 'New and unused machinery used in a process of manufacture … depreciable at the rate of 40% in the first year of use and 20% in the three following years'; used machinery 20% a year over five years (PwC). Average over the 4 years = 100/4 = 25%.
items.notes: Value is the 4-year average (derived); the actual profile is 40/20/20/20.

items.basis: 'on average, the employer's share of contributions represents 45% of the gross salary' (PwC): sickness/maternity, old age, family, work accident, unemployment, AGIRC-ARRCO, etc.
items.notes: Average only; general reduction on wages up to 1.6× SMIC lowers it a lot for low wages, ceilings lower it for high wages.

items.basis: 'the overall social security burden … around 40% of gross remuneration, with approximately 30% borne by the employer' (PwC). INPS rates vary by sector, size, category.
items.notes: Excludes TFR severance accrual (6.91%) and INAIL premium.

items.basis: 'general contribution rates are … 30.65% for employers, plus a variable rate for occupational accidents (e.g. 1.50% for office work)'; base min EUR 1,424.40 / max EUR 5,101.20 a month in 2026 (PwC). Common contingencies 23.6 + unemployment 5.5 + FOGASA 0.2 + training 0.6 + MEI 0.75.
items.notes: Component split is from memory (sums to 30.65); manufacturing AT/EP premium is higher than the office 1.5%.

items.basis: 'contributions are due … at rates of 11% and 23.75% by the employee and the employer'; plus a compulsory occupational-accident insurance premium (PwC).
'The employer: 24.8% for social security and 9% for health insurance'; social security base capped at 48× average wage (CZK 2,350,416 for 2026), health uncapped (PwC). 24.8 + 9 = 33.8.
Employer: 'Work insurance contribution: 2.25%'; social insurance 4%/8% only for uncommon/special work conditions; none for normal conditions (PwC). Employees bear 25% + 10%.
'Social security contributions are levied at 31.42% of the total taxable remuneration (no cap)' (PwC).

Belastingdienst 2026 Tabel 9: AWf laag 2.74% (hoog 7.74%), Aof laag 6.27% / hoog 7.63%, opslag Wko 0.50%, Ufo 0.68%, Whk per employer; werkgeversheffing Zvw 6.10%. Large employer, permanent contracts: 2.74 + 7.63 + 0.50 + 0.68 + 6.10 = 17.65% (small employer 16.29%), plus Whk (WGA + ZW-flex, by sector ~1–2%). Capped at the max premium wage EUR 79,409 (PwC).
items.scope: employer employee-insurance premiums + Zvw, before Whk
items.notes: Sum is derived; Whk sector rate for metal industry not read. Flex contracts take AWf hoog (+5 points).

items.basis: 'The employer's share currently varies around 27%' (PwC); no cap.
items.notes: Approximate (basic 25% + wage moderation etc.); structural reductions apply.

items.basis: Employer social security 24.4% (cap EUR 16,764/month) + accident insurance 0.8% (uncapped) + health 11% (uncapped) (PwC). 24.4 + 0.8 + 11 = 36.2.
Employer 16.10% (pension 8.85, health 6.56, unemployment 0.06, injury 0.53, parental 0.10) + long-term care 1% from 1 July 2025 (PwC). 16.10 + 1 = 17.10.

Employer social security 1.77%–3.03% (2.49–3.75% for fixed-term contracts) by risk category, incl. Guarantee Fund and Long-term Employment Fund 0.16% each; capped at 60 average wages (EUR 138,729 in 2026) (PwC).
items.notes: Employees bear 19.5%. Manufacturing risk category not determined.

items.basis: Employer social security 14.12%–14.82% (by work-accident risk) + health 4.8% = 18.92%–19.62%; max insurance base EUR 2,111.64/month (to 31 Jul 2026), EUR 2,300 from 1 Aug 2026 (PwC).

Social security employer 20.98% (sickness 3.78, unemployment 2.95, pension 12.55, accident 1.10, misc 0.60; cap EUR 6,930/month) + Family Burdens Equalisation Levy 3.7% + municipal payroll tax 3% + Chamber contribution 0.31–0.40% + employee pension fund (MV) 1.53% (PwC). 20.98 + 3.7 + 3 + 0.40 + 1.53 = 29.61 (29.52 at 0.31).
items.scope: employer total incl. payroll levies, below the cap
items.notes: Derived sum; Vienna adds EUR 2/week/employee.

items.basis: Employer: pension and disability 10% + health 5.15%; base min 35.05% of average wage, max 5× average wage (PwC). 10 + 5.15 = 15.15.

Social security employer general rate 20.75% (reduced by 5 points in manufacturing if conditions met: 15.75%) + unemployment insurance employer 2%; base TRY 33,030–297,270/month from 1 Jan 2026 (PwC). 20.75 + 2 = 22.75 (17.75 with the manufacturing reduction).

Employer social security 6.2% on the first USD 184,500 (2026) + Medicare 1.45% on all wages; FUTA 6% on the first USD 7,000, reducible by up to 5.4% (net 0.6%); plus state unemployment (SUI) and workers' compensation at state/industry rates (PwC).
items.notes: FUTA net 0.6% × USD 7,000 = USD 42 a year; SUI varies by state and experience.

items.basis: Employer CPP and EI: 2026 maxima CAD 4,646.45 (CPP) and EI matching 1.4× the employee premium (PwC). Derived: CPP 5.95% × (YMPE 74,600 − 3,500) = 4,230.45 + CPP2 4% × (85,000 − 74,600) = 416 → 4,646.45 ✓; EI employee 1.63% × 68,900 = 1,123.07 ✓, employer 1.4 × 1.63 = 2.282%. 5.95 + 2.282 = 8.23% below the YMPE.
items.kind: advisory summary (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries) (rates derived from published maxima)
items.scope: federal CPP + EI, outside Quebec, below the YMPE
items.notes: Rates are back-solved (reconcile exactly to PwC maxima) but not read on a page. Add provincial payroll tax (ON EHT up to 1.95%; 1.95–4.3% across provinces) and workers' compensation. PwC corporate page lists the employer EI maximum as CAD 1,123.07, which is the EMPLOYEE maximum — looks wrong (1.4× = CAD 1,572.30).

items.basis: IMSS / INFONAVIT / SAR: employer maximum annual contribution MXN 227,286 (low-risk company) on wages above MXN 1,070,155 a year; includes retirement 2% and housing 5% (PwC). Derived 227,286 / 1,070,155 = 21.24%.
items.scope: employer effective rate at the cap, low risk class
items.notes: At ordinary wages the rate differs (fixed quota on the UMA, progressive cesantía y vejez); occupational risk premium varies. Excludes 10% PTU profit sharing and state payroll tax (2–3%).

items.basis: Employer INSS 20% on payroll (22.5% some sectors) + FGTS 8% (PwC), plus RAT work-accident 1–3% × FAP and 'third parties' (SENAI, SESI, INCRA, salário-educação …) at a rate depending on activity — not given on the page. 20 + 8 = 28.
items.notes: Typical industrial total with RAT and third parties is ~35–37% (not sourced here).

items.basis: Employer share (Tokyo): health 4.925% from Mar 2026 (cap JPY 1.39m/month), child and childcare support 0.115%, welfare pension 9.15% (cap JPY 650k/month), child allowance 0.36% (employer only), employment insurance 0.9% (employer, from Apr 2025), plus workers' accident insurance by industry (PwC individual + corporate pages). 4.925 + 0.115 + 9.15 + 0.36 + 0.9 = 15.45.
items.scope: employer total excl. workers' accident insurance, age < 40
items.notes: PwC's corporate page still shows health 4.955% (Mar 2025) and 0.9% employment insurance from Apr 2025; the April 2026 employer employment-insurance rate was not found. Long-term care 0.81% each for ages 40–64.

items.basis: Employer: National Pension 4.75% (cap KRW 6.59m/month from Jul 2026), NHI incl. long-term care ~4.0674%, Employment Insurance 1.15%–1.75% (by size), Workers' Compensation 0.56%–18.56% by industry (PwC). 4.75 + 4.0674 + 1.15 = 9.97 (10.57 at 1.75), before WCI.

Employer: labour insurance (11.5% ordinary + 1% employment) × 70% = 8.75% (cap TWD 45,800); NHI 5.17% × 60% × 1.56 headcount = 4.839% (cap TWD 313,000); labour pension ≥ 6% (cap TWD 150,000) (PwC). 8.75 + 4.839 + 6 = 19.59.
items.scope: employer total, domestic employee, below caps
items.notes: Excludes occupational accident insurance and wage-arrears fund (not on page); 2.11% supplementary NHI premium on pay above insured salary.

items.basis: 'All employees are required to contribute … 5% of their salary, up to a maximum contribution of THB 875 per month. Employers and the government are also required to contribute an equal amount' (PwC).
items.scope: employer social security fund, capped at THB 875/month
items.notes: Cap THB 875 = 5% × THB 17,500 wage base. Workmen's compensation fund extra.

items.basis: Employer: social insurance 17.5% + health insurance 3% + unemployment insurance 1%; SI/HI capped at 20× reference level, UI at 20× regional minimum wage (PwC). 17.5 + 3 + 1 = 21.5.
items.notes: Excludes 2% trade union fee.

items.basis: EPF employer 13% (wages ≤ MYR 5,000; 12% above), Employment Insurance System 0.2% (max MYR 11.90), SOCSO EIS + IS employer contribution (max MYR 104.15/month; table rate ~1.75%, not on page) (PwC). 13 + 0.2 + 1.75 = 14.95.
items.notes: SOCSO 1.75% is the PERKESO table rate from memory — verify. HRDF levy 1% for employers with ≥ 10 staff (not read in full).

items.basis: BPJS employer: work accident 0.24–1.74%, death 0.3%, old age saving 3.7%, healthcare 4% (base cap), pension 2% (base cap) (PwC). 0.24 + 0.3 + 3.7 + 4 + 2 = 10.24% to 11.74%.

Employer maxima: SSS PHP 2,000 + mandatory provident fund PHP 1,500 + EC PHP 30 per month; HDMF and PHIC equal to the employee amounts (max PHP 200 and PHP 2,500) (PwC). Rates behind those maxima: SSS 10% of MSC (3,500 / 35,000), PhilHealth 2.5% (2,500 / 100,000), Pag-IBIG 2% (200 / 10,000) = 14.5% + EC.
items.kind: advisory summary (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries) (rates back-solved from maxima)
items.notes: Salary caps (MSC 35,000, PHIC ceiling 100,000, HDMF 10,000) are from memory — verify.

items.basis: CPF: 'Employers and employees contribute 17% and 20%, respectively, of monthly ordinary wages (OW), up to an OW ceiling of SGD 8,000' (citizens/PRs ≤ 55) (PwC).
items.notes: Foreigners: no CPF (foreign worker levy instead). Skills Development Levy 0.25% extra (not read).

items.basis: CNSS employer: family allocation 6.40%, social allocation 8.98% (capped at MAD 6,000/month), professional training 1.60%, mandatory medical care 4.11% (PwC). 6.40 + 8.98 + 1.60 + 4.11 = 21.09.

items.notes: Work-accident insurance and TFP / FOPROLOS payroll taxes not included.
